text:
incident-bot: Pager: GeoDNS anomalies detected — high NXDOMAIN and resolver error rates for eu-west and ap-south regions. 5xx from external resolvers up 28% in last 5m. Potential Route53/Cloudflare divergence. Auto-ticket created: INC-2026-4310. :rotating_light:

oncall-jordan: I'm awake. Acknowledging. Priorities: confirm customer impact, start mitigation, escalate to netops if it's external.

alice-infra: Seeing split answers from our GeoDNS fronting domain. Dig from eu-west1 vs us-east1 returns different TTLs and some NXDOMAIN. Example:```
; eu-west1
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 app.redwood-inference.com A
192.0.2.11
```
vs
```
; from ap-south
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 app.redwood-inference.com A
<empty> ;; NXDOMAIN
``
Route53 health checks show intermittent failing for the primary geodns endpoints, but Route53 console still has primary as weighted 100%.

ravi-netops: I just opened a Cloudflare ticket (CF-987654). CF console shows recent resolver anomalies in their APAC edge. Cloudflare status page: https://status.cloudflare.com/incident/abcdef — they acknowledge partial outage in APAC resolvers.

megan-sre: Customer impact telemetry: 5% of API requests from APAC are getting 502s (ingress layer) and client-side DNS failures up ~12% last 10m. Incidents dashboard: https://grafana.internal/incidents/geo-dns — I pinned the error spike.

liz-pm: Which customer segments are impacted? Any paying customers hitting SLAs? Need a short summary for comms.

carlos-ops: Quick confirmation: this looks like a resolver-level issue (clients can't resolve primary records). Mitigation options: 1) change Route53 failover policy to route to secondary records (lower TTL) 2) temporarily add an A record in a different zone as emergency fallback 3) ask Cloudflare to failover/resync.

oncall-jordan: Let's do 1) and 3) simultaneously. Megan, can you kick off an automated reroute to secondary? Alice, prep the Route53 change and I will approve. Ravi, keep CF ticket hot and request bypass/routing fix.

alice-infra: Preparing change batch. Proposed change (dry-run):
```json
{
  "Comment": "Emergency geo failover — route APAC to fallback pool",
  "Changes": [
    {
      "Action": "UPSERT",
      "ResourceRecordSet": {
        "Name": "app.redwood-inference.com.",
        "Type": "A",
        "SetIdentifier": "apac-fallback",
        "Weight": 1,
        "TTL": 30,
        "ResourceRecords": [{ "Value": "198.51.100.23" }]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
Will run after +1 from Jordan. Note: TTL=30 to minimize propagation window.

oncall-jordan: +1. Run it and post the change-id here. Also set health-check re-eval to 10s if possible.

alice-infra: Executing now: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z3EXAMPLE --change-batch file://apac-fallback.json` ChangeId: C1234567890.

deploy-bot: Change C1234567890 has been applied to route53 (status: PENDING).

megan-sre: After the change, I'm seeing initial drop in NXDOMAIN from APAC resolvers; error rate down to 8% in the first 60s. Monitoring continuing.

ravi-netops: Cloudflare responded in the ticket: "We have mitigations rolling; some edge resolvers are being rebalanced. Recommend keeping your fallback in place until the fix is complete." CF rep asked for packet captures — I uploaded a sample.

liz-pm: Draft for status update to customers (short): "We are investigating resolution failures impacting DNS lookups in APAC. We deployed an emergency routing fallback to restore availability while external resolver providers apply fixes. We will update in 30 minutes." Thoughts?

carlos-ops: Sounds good. Add an ETA note: investigating, mitigation in place, no data loss, some requests may see degraded performance.

megan-sre: Add the affected regions and rough percent: APAC ~5-10% requests impacted, EU splice saw brief blips but mostly stable.

liz-pm: Posted customer status update on status.redwood.com and notified account teams.

oncall-jordan: Okay switching to handoff: I'm paged again inbound. Emma, can you take the next 30m? I'll summarize context. @oncall-emma

oncall-emma: Taking it. Thanks Jordan — will monitor CF ticket, Route53 change status, and client error rates. Please leave any open follow-ups.

oncall-jordan: Notes for handoff: ChangeId C1234567890 (apac fallback) is applied. Cloudflare CF-987654 ongoing; Luca from CF assigned. Watch for TTL expiry (30s) and confirm 200s from clients. If error >5% for 10m, escalate to oncall-tier2.

megan-sre: Adding runbook checklist to the thread for Emma: 1) Verify Route53 change status broad-apply 2) Watch Grafana panel (link) 3) Confirm CF ticket progress 4) If reversion needed, run rollback command (aws cli example below).

alice-infra: Rollback command (if needed):
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z3EXAMPLE --change-batch file://rollback.json
```
Make sure to include the original ResourceRecordSet payload.

cloudflare-support: Cloudflare update: "Mitigation applied; edge resolver cluster in APAC showing steady state. Propagation to public resolvers may take up to 5 minutes. Continue to use your fallback until metrics are green."

oncall-emma: Seeing steady improvements — NXDOMAIN down to baseline in ap-south after ~4m. Monitoring shows request success back to normal.

megan-sre: Error budget impact assessment: short blip; we anticipate <0.01% monthly SLA impact for paying customers. I'll add the event to the incident timeline for postmortem.

alice-infra: Rolling TTL back to 300s and removing apac fallback in 10m unless we see regression. Scheduling change: `aws ...` placeholder.

deploy-bot: Change C1234567890 has transitioned to INSYNC.

liz-pm: Great work. I'll start the incident summary draft for the internal postmortem: cause: external resolver cluster degradation (Cloudflare APAC); impact: DNS resolution failures for subset of APAC clients causing 502s; mitigation: emergency Route53 fallback to secondary IPs, CF mitigations; next steps: review TTL/health-check config and add automated fallback playbook.

oncall-emma: I will keep monitoring for 20 more minutes and then close the thread if stable. Leaving note: assigned follow-up to alice-infra to run a post-incident runbook and to megan-sre for SLA calc.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-4310 status: Mitigated -> Monitoring. Assigned: alice-infra, megan-sre.

megan-sre: Closing notes in 20m. All telemetry looks green at last check.

oncall-emma: Closing thread — resolved for now. Will open a postmortem doc and tag stakeholders. :white_check_mark:
